    The Artemis II mission uses the Space Launch System (SLS) rocket, which stands 322 feet (98 meters) tall when fully stacked with the Orion spacecraft. This height makes it taller than the Statue of Liberty and comparable to a 30-story building. 
    • Total Height: 322 feet (
      ).
    • Rocket Components: The SLS rocket itself, including boosters, is ~322 ft.
    • Comparison: The rocket is about 7 feet taller than London's Big Ben. 
    The Artemis II crew, consisting of four astronauts, launched from NASA's Kennedy Space Center aboard this vehicle for a 10-day mission around the Moon.

    What is the tallest rocket ever built?
    An AI Overview is not available for this searchCan't generate an AI overview right now. Try again later.
    AI Overview
    SpaceX's Starship is the tallest rocket ever built, standing at nearly 120–123 meters (394–404 feet) tall, surpassing the 363-foot (110-meter) Saturn V. It is designed for full reusability and significantly higher payload capacity than any previous rocket. 
    This video shows how SpaceX's Starship compares in size to other rockets:
    0:45
    Cleo Abram
    YouTube• Mar 18, 2025
    Key Details of Top Tallest Rockets:
     
    • SpaceX Starship: ~120–123 meters (394–404 ft).
    • Saturn V (NASA): 110.6 meters (363 ft).
    • SLS (NASA Artemis): ~98 meters (322 ft). 
    Key Facts about the Tallest Rocket (Starship): 
    • Structure: Consists of a 33-engine Super Heavy booster and the Starship spacecraft.
    • Capacity: Designed to carry over 100 passengers and 150 tons of cargo, or more, to space.
    • Future Height: Future versions of Starship are anticipated to reach 140 meters in height, according to Elon Musk.
